A grown-up-sized long-sleeved, ankle-length, drop-hood zip-front onesie, with a big attached hood, with plain ribbed cuffs and no gloves, and footless, ending in plain ankle cuffs with bare feet, in bamboo-blend jersey, a real plain stretch suit and not a real garment, covered edge to edge in a high-detail print that runs onto the sleeves and around the back, designed to make the onesie look like the outfit of a wasteland raider. The whole suit is the outfit, front, back, arms and legs (and any hood, gloves or feet) are printed as the matching parts of it, with the seams and the zip hidden in the pattern. The print shows spiked shoulder pads over bare arms, torn trousers, with a skull mask printed on the hood, with no footwear shown because the suit is footless, and the sleeves end in plain cuffs with no hands printed. Front and back are both fully printed, the back showing how the outfit looks from behind. There is no separate background, the print is cut to the onesie's shape. Every sleeve and every leg of the suit is a tube covered completely, all the way round, in the outfit's cloth for that limb (sleeve cloth, trouser, tights or leg fabric), so no grey, blue or coloured background shows on the arms, legs, sides or back. No limbs are printed on the suit, bare arms and legs are never drawn as skin on the fabric, and the suit is simply cut short or sleeveless wherever the outfit would show them. Every part of the shirt, shoulders and sleeves included, shows the outfit's own colours and cloth texture in one uniform print. The print is cut exactly to the suit, neck, shoulders, armholes, sleeves and hem are all covered in the outfit's own fabric. The outline is exactly a onesie's, nothing sticks out past the suit's edges, and no coat tails, skirts, capes, extra sleeves or loose layers hang outside it. The outfit is stretched to the suit's own straight-sided shape and fills it completely, so it suits any body size. The printed parts are flat ink on stretch jersey. No standing figure, torso, arms or legs are depicted; the suit's own shape is the body, and the print is only the outfit's fabric covering it from edge to edge. The outfit has bare arms on the forearm and wrist, so the onesie's sleeves run to the wrist and the printed bare arms sit at the sleeve ends, with nothing beyond the cuffs. The printed top of torn trousers reaching the hem and ending there. Raised plush layers are sewn on over the print, the hood trim in fleece, the collar and lapels in quilted padding and the belt and buckle in velvet, standing out from the surface. The print gives the whole outfit, and raised layers of soft fabric are sewn on over it for the collar, pockets, belt, buttons and patches, so the suit is half picture and half sculpture. It is a complete costume of wasteland raider in one piece, shown full length from collar to ankles, spiked shoulder pads over bare arms, torn trousers on the legs, a skull mask (as the hood), boots (as the feet), a chain sewn or attached to the suit. The upper half carries the top and the leg tubes carry the lower garment, so the whole outfit reads at once. Novelty embellishments, metallic foil-print accents that catch the light, a quilted belt-like waist band with a big buckle shape, satin ribbon bows and piping and padded 3D patch pockets. The uniform fills the whole straight-sided suit shape edge to edge, the same width at chest, waist and hem. The printed parts are flat ink on stretch jersey. The print shows a heavy mail coat with a fur mantle, trousers, with a horned crown printed on the hood, with no footwear shown because the suit is footless, and printed gloves on the attached gloves at the sleeve ends. Front and back are both fully printed, the back showing how the outfit looks from behind. The outfit's own cloth reaches every seam, cuff and hem with no border or backdrop. The outfit's cloth wraps the whole suit like a pattern, with the body, the outside and inside of each sleeve and each leg, and the sides, so there are no plain coloured side panels or background patches anywhere. Where the outfit leaves arms or legs bare, the suit itself is cut sleeveless, short-sleeved or short-legged at that point, so the wearer's own limbs show; no printed arm, leg, hand, foot or skin appears on the suit's fabric. Every part of the shirt, shoulders and sleeves included, shows the outfit's own colours and cloth texture in one uniform print. The outfit's cloth runs unbroken from the collar band across both shoulders and down both sleeves to their hems, so every part of the suit is outfit cloth. The outline is exactly a onesie's, nothing sticks out past the suit's edges, and no coat tails, skirts, capes, extra sleeves or loose layers hang outside it. The uniform fills the whole straight-sided suit shape edge to edge, the same width at chest, waist and hem. The printed parts are flat ink on stretch jersey. No standing figure, torso, arms or legs are depicted; the suit's own shape is the body, and the print is only the outfit's fabric covering it from edge to edge. Raised plush layers are sewn on over the print, the straps and holsters in quilted padding, the pockets in faux fur and the buttons in velvet, standing out from the surface. The print gives the whole outfit, and raised layers of soft fabric are sewn on over it for the collar, pockets, belt, buttons and patches, so the suit is half picture and half sculpture. The suit is the whole dwarf king outfit, not just a top, with a heavy mail coat with a fur mantle, trousers on the legs, a horned crown (as the hood), boots (as the feet), a battle axe sewn or attached to the suit. It is shown in full, from the neckline down to the ankle cuffs. Novelty embellishments, oversized novelty buttons in contrasting colours, scalloped felt edging, dangling fabric tassels on the zip pull and hood and iridescent shimmer-mesh overlays. The embellishments are sewn on as real raised fabric, so the suit has depth, texture and sparkle from every angle.

The hood carries only hood cloth, no face, hair, ears or head is printed on it, and no crowd, audience, stage, lights or scene appears anywhere on the suit, only the outfit's own cloth. Raised plush layers are sewn on over the print, the collar and lapels in velvet, the straps and holsters in faux leather and the belt and buckle in felt, standing out from the surface. A printed base shows the full outfit, while felt, fleece and faux-leather pieces are stitched over the key details to give them real depth. A full goblin trader costume, head to toe in a single suit, with a patchwork vest with pouches, ragged trousers on the legs, a floppy hat (as the hood), boots (as the feet), a sack sewn or attached to the suit. Nothing of the outfit is missing and the legs of the suit show the lower garment. Novelty embellishments, satin ribbon bows and piping, dangling fabric tassels on the zip pull and hood, glitter-flecked tulle layered at the hem and embroidered patches and crests with stitched borders. Everything is chosen to be fun to look at and tactile to feel, bumpy, fluffy, shiny and soft in turn.

The whole suit is the outfit, front, back, arms and legs (and any hood, gloves or feet) are printed as the matching parts of it, with the seams and the zip hidden in the pattern. The shirt's sleeves are tailored to end about two-thirds of the way down the arm, exactly where the outfit's sleeves end.
